attacks.claim: Retrieval moves to Nimbus Vector Store, provisioned only in us-east-2 (EU on a roadmap), while the DPAs require all customer documents and derived data (chunks, embeddings) to be processed and stored in the EU. Week 2 re-embedding of ~41M chunks and dual-write, then week 4 cutover, would place customer-derived data in the US, with no EU-region gate or fallback.
attacks.evidence: "Vector Store is in public preview and currently provisioned in us-east-2, with EU regions on Nimbus's GA roadmap." / "Week 2: re-embed corpus (~41M chunks) into Nimbus Vector Store; dual-write new documents."

attacks.claim: Week 3 irreversibly releases the A100 reservation and deletes the fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters before the week-4 cutover and before any regression run. Week 5 then removes pgvector and vLLM manifests. No rollback path to the known-good stack remains if Nimbus quality, latency, or residency fails, and no archive or retention step is stated.
attacks.evidence: "Week 3: release the A100 reservation ... and delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage"; "Week 5: remove pgvector, vLLM manifests, and GPU node pool from Terraform."

attacks.claim: The agreed constraint makes the 4,100-case regression suite the release gate for any model change. The plan defers it to week 6+, after cutover and the irreversible deletions, justified by a 25-question sample that cannot establish parity. The plan ships a model change and LoRA-to-prompt rewrite to all tenants without passing the gate and documents no waiver.
attacks.evidence: "This confirms quality parity or better, so the full regression suite run moves to post-migration hardening (week 6+) rather than blocking cutover."

attacks.claim: Quality evidence is weak: 25 support-inbox questions, two raters, with the tally leaving 3 of 25 unaccounted for. It is not stated whether the tested configuration used the new per-practice system prompts. Replacing LoRA practice-area behaviour with prompts is unvalidated before cutover.
attacks.evidence: "Atlas-L was preferred in 19 of 25 and tied in 3." / "practice-area behaviour that lived in LoRA adapters moves into per-practice system prompts (drafted in week 1 by the applied team)."

attacks.claim: Zero data retention and the EU region are stated only for the generation Inference API. No ZDR or EU-residency terms are shown for embed-3 or Vector Store, both of which receive customer content and derived data.
attacks.evidence: "Zero data retention is enabled on our org account (signed addendum, ref NMB-ZDR-2291)." ABSENT: region/ZDR coverage for embed-3 and Vector Store

attacks.claim: Nimbus becomes a new sub-processor of customer data, but the timeline has no step for customer notification, DPA sub-processor list updates, or deletion of customer data from old stores. The plan also does not say how the 25 support-inbox questions sent to Nimbus were handled.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no sub-processor notification, DPA amendment, or deletion-propagation step in sections 5 and 7.

attacks.claim: Releasing the GPU reservation in week 3 precedes the week-4 cutover, so the plan does not say what serves production generation during that window. Dual-write covers only new documents, so updates and deletions during the re-embed window are not propagated or reconciled, and there is no retrieval-parity check.
attacks.evidence: "Week 3: release the A100 reservation" vs "Week 4: cut all tenants over"; "dual-write new documents"

attacks.claim: Re-embedding ~41M chunks in one week (~68 chunks/s average) has no batching or rate-limit budget and risks contending with the 120 req/s contracted limit alongside ~40 req/s production traffic. The Vector Store (preview) has no stated collection-count or size limits.
attacks.evidence: "Week 2: re-embed corpus (~41M chunks)..." and "our peak is ~40 req/s; our contracted tier allows 120 req/s."

attacks.claim: Tenant isolation relies on per-tenant collections and tenant-scoped keys in a preview managed service, with no cross-tenant isolation test in the timeline. This is critical for law-firm confidentiality.
attacks.evidence: "Tenant isolation in Vector Store uses one collection per tenant with a tenant-scoped API key"; ABSENT: isolation test task in the timeline

attacks.claim: No monitoring, SLOs, alerting, timeout/retry/429 handling, or fallback is defined for the new managed dependencies, a preview service among them, and the plan cuts all tenants over at once with no canary or feature flag.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: dashboards, alerts, retry/timeout policy, canary; "Week 4: cut all tenants over to Nimbus"

attacks.claim: The $7,900/mo generation estimate has no stated token-volume basis and ignores that 200k context raises per-request tokens. There are no spend guardrails, and one-time re-embed and dual-run costs are not in the table.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus generation (est.) | $0 | $7,900"; ABSENT: token volume, budget cap, re-embed cost

attacks.claim: Latency was measured from Frankfurt pods, but the target region is Dublin, and only TTFT was measured, not total generation time at long context.
attacks.evidence: "Atlas-L p95 time-to-first-token measured at 640 ms from our Frankfurt pods (1,000 requests, week of 10-05)"
